doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: How Duke Ellington's 70th birthday at the Nixon White House came about
summary: Hinton explains Nixon's aide proposed honoring Ellington, who was invited among friends, with players such as Earl Hines and Louie Bellson.

blocks.x: I’ve just got to mention about you, man. I’ve seen you under every kind of circumstances and you amaze me, how you can take over and make the punishment fit the crime. And I’m thinking now, on Duke Ellington’s 70th birthday in the White House, this was a magnificent, and the public should know how that came about. Nixon was having a lot of trouble with the black community.

Yes. He couldn’t you know, he didn’t vote for us, we didn’t vote for him, and he didn’t do a damn thing for us. So it was just that way. So he was having a lot of trouble in the White House, and one of his assistants, used to be a clarinet player, can’t recall his name, he was an assistant to Nixon, he said, “What do you think I could do to kind of get the favor of the black folks community?” He said, “Look if you give Duke Ellington the Medal of Freedom, and give a party in the White House for him, everybody loves Duke. See that might kind of cool it out.” He said well go ahead and do that. So that’s how that thing came about.
I thought Willis had something to do with that.
Willis Conover. The clarinet player, what was his name? He was an assistant, he used to play the clarinet in Woody Herman’s band.
That’s great to know that we have a mole in the White House for jazz.
That’s right. So he organized it. And we got together Duke Ellington’s friends. I don’t think there had ever been that many black folks in the White House at any one time ever.
Yeah, but I loved it because there were white people there too.
Of course, there are always white people there.
But I mean like Bill Berry was in the band, Urbie Green, Gerry Mulligan.
But I’m not talking about the band, I was talking about the public, Duke Ellington’s friends.
Your wife was there, my wife was there, Basie’s wife was there. Woody and Lionel was there. The band was —
Oh, yeah, friends of Ellington. Yeah.
There was five piano players, you remember? Five piano players. Willie “The Lion”, Earl Hines, Marian McPartland, and Hank Jones. And the drummer was Louie Bellson. Jim Hall was the guitar player—
